question.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that  its  unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}⟩\,.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature: 

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,-\frac{4}{5}(-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{8}{25}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\frac{8}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{8}{25}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{8}{25}\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}))}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{8}{25})}=\frac{25}{8}.
$$
